codes.doc: `cdm` is not the major version of this definition.
A registered invariant check threw or reported a code it did not declare; the document is refused unchecked.
Content on a node type that has none.
A text node without text.
The envelope has a member other than `cdm`, `requires` and `doc`; metadata belongs to the document resource.
A node, mark, attribute or value of a feature that `requires` does not list.
A footnote with more than one paragraph; version 1 allows one (CDM-001).
A member of the wrong JSON type: `attrs` not an object, `content` or `marks` not an array, a child that is no node.
A block that carries marks. Block suggestions are entries of the suggest attribute of a paragraph, a table row or a table, not marks (03 §5).
The document, or a node, is not a JSON object.
The document has no canonical form (03 §2).
A node that exists only in projections (ADR 0019), such as `hidden_region`.
The redaction marker of projections (ADR 0019) in a stored value.
`requires` is not an array, names an unknown feature, or names one twice.
The ProseMirror schema refuses the content: an order or a count its content expression does not allow.
`doc` is not a node of the top type.
An attribute the node or mark does not declare.
A mark type the definition does not have.
A node or mark member other than its own.
A node type the definition does not have.
Two nodes share an identifier.
The commit changed a non-null identifier.
A node type that declares an `id` has none.
One suggestion identifier with two users; an identifier belongs to the user who first used it (03 §5).
A region or a section break that is not a direct child of the body.
A region inside a region.
A region identifier that was removed earlier.
An asset that is not attached to the document.
A bookmark name or an equation label used twice, which makes references to it ambiguous.
A field target that names nothing, or not something a reference can target.
A numbering level that the numbering definition does not have.
A reference to a definition that does not exist.
A reference to a definition of the wrong kind, such as a character style as a paragraph style.
A `basedOn` chain with a cycle.
A `basedOn` chain of more than ten styles.
`headerRows` larger than the number of rows.
A table row whose spans, with the columns covered from rows above, do not cover the grid exactly.
A row span that runs past the last row.
A canonical size above 16 MiB.
A `latex` attribute longer than 4,000 characters, or a table grid of more than 63 columns.
Nesting deeper than 12.
More than 500 regions.
The math gate of 09 refused a `latex` value.
A link whose `href` is not http, https, mailto or an in-document target.
A page or column break inside a table cell, a caption or a footnote.
A figure with `placement: float` inside a table cell.
A footnote inside a caption.
A footnote inside a footnote.
A form field inside a header, a footer or a footnote (12 §3.2).
A table inside a story or a footnote.
An attribute value outside its grammar: type, range, length, pattern or size.
A required attribute is null or absent.
Two options of one choice field share an identifier.
A field target not in the form its kind needs, a missing target where the kind needs one, or a target or sequence name on a kind that takes none.
A `fmt` suggestion whose `before` is not the shape of CDM-002, or names attributes a block suggestion cannot change.
Preserved inline content with neither its fragment asset nor the tree of a small marker.
A built-in style identifier used by another style, or `builtIn` on a style without one.
A table property (`cellMargins`, `headerRowShading`, `bandedRows`, inside borders) on a style that is not a table style.
A table of contents whose `minLevel` exceeds `maxLevel`.
An extension node whose name, payload or fallback is outside its grammar, or whose payload is above its limit.
An extension node without the fallback it needs: a picture or a text for a block, a text for an inline.
Two form fields share a key.
A field `assignee` that names no `role_def`, for example after the role was deleted.
A `formValue` field whose target names no form field key, for example after the field was deleted.
More than 2,000 form fields.
More than 500 rules.
A field value of more than 4 KiB.
A field value that does not have the type of its kind.
